Class CausalQuiesce

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalQuiesce
public final class CausalQuiesce extends Object
A shared handle for coordinating graceful shutdown across every causal task in one application instance. Register the same CausalQuiesce with every CausalProcessors / CausalStreams builder whose tasks should participate, then, from your own shutdown path (e.g. a signal handler), call requestQuiesce() and poll isSafeToClose() before calling KafkaStreams#close: 
CausalQuiesce quiesce = CausalQuiesce.create();
// ... pass quiesce to every CausalProcessors/CausalStreams builder via withQuiesce(quiesce) ...
Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(new Thread(() -> {
    quiesce.requestQuiesce();
    while (!quiesce.isSafeToClose()) {
        Thread.sleep(100);
    }
    streams.close();
}));

A task registered with a CausalQuiesce keeps processing normally after requestQuiesce() — nothing about how it delivers or forwards records changes. It only reports itself drained once its causal buffer has emptied through the ordinary delivery path (a held record's dependencies becoming satisfied by a later message, exactly as it would without quiesce), so no synthetic completeness is ever fabricated to force this. isSafeToClose() becomes true once quiesce has been requested and every currently registered task is drained.

This is a stall-avoidance optimization, not a correctness requirement. Every held record is already changelog-backed and survives an ungraceful stop; closing without ever calling requestQuiesce() loses nothing but resumes with a non-empty buffer to replay.

Thread-safety: safe to share across every task/partition's own Kafka Streams thread, and to poll from an unrelated shutdown thread.
